item.title: FACING REALITY: Simple fact - you can't reach the First World with a Third World mentality
item.description: THERE'S a phrase that gets tossed around casually in Caribbean conversations: “third world.”

item.title: Students strengthen leadership skills at youth governance workshop
item.description: STUDENTS from across New Providence came together to strengthen their leadership skills and deepen their understanding of governance, civic participation, and national development during the Youth in Governance Capacity Building Workshop.

item.title: Bahamas ‘in far darker place’ in unregulated medicine sale
item.description: The Bahamas is in “a far darker place than a decade ago” over the sale of unapproved and ‘grey market’ medicines, an ex-health minister asserted yesterday, adding: “The pirates are still here.”

item.title: 'Uber coming' despite taxi union resistance
item.description: A BUSINESSMAN says he is bringing Uber to the country despite resounding opposition from the Bahamas Taxi Cab Union.

item.title: 'It looked like he was begging for his life'
item.description: DEANGELO “Ducky” Burrows was shot seven times on a Grand Bahama street Saturday night, wounds his family says suggest he was begging for his life.

item.title: Unlawfully detained Guyanese man awarded $75K settlement
item.description: A SUPREME Court judge has ruled that a Guyanese man was unlawfully detained for more than three months in 2006 under an invalid deportation order and in conditions that breached his constitutional rights, awarding him $75,000 in damages but rejecting his claims that his later arrest, prosecution and year-long imprisonment on bribery charges were unlawful.

item.title: FNM demands answers after BGC 'denied access' during blackout
item.description: FREE National Movement Senator Michela Barnett-Ellis is demanding answers from the Davis administration following claims by Bahamas Grid Company (BGC) that it was denied access to the New Providence Control Center during the weekend’s island-wide power outage.

item.title: The quiet victims - kids left behind by murder
item.description: AS a new month begins, some children in The Bahamas are still learning how to live without a mother or father taken by murder — and the relatives now raising them are doing so while grieving themselves.

item.title: FOAM president says celebrate your birthday by donating blood
item.description: NEARLY every day, another flyer circulates appealing for blood donations for someone in need — young or old — a reality that has prompted Khandi Gibson, president of Families of All Murder Victims (FOAM), to challenge the public to mark their birthdays by giving a pint of blood.

item.title: Repeat offender accused of theft at Dr Duane Sands' home
item.description: A REPEAT offender accused of stealing from and trespassing on the property of FNM chairman Dr Duane Sands was remanded to prison yesterday.
